questions.subject: Descriptive English
questions.prompt: Write an essay in 250–300 words on: Artificial Intelligence and Employment: Threat or Opportunity for India's Workforce?

content.text: Unofficial practice rubric (/20): relevance and content 7; analysis and balance 5; organisation and coherence 4; language, grammar and expression 4. This is a manually assessed Day 2 practice essay; the topic and limits are practice specifications, not a claim about the official 2026 paper's exact word limit.

questions.subject: PFRDA Act
questions.prompt: Under the PFRDA Act, 2013, an eligible person aggrieved by an appealable order of the Authority ordinarily appeals first to which forum?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Section 37 provides the appeal from an appealable PFRDA order to the Securities Appellate Tribunal; the other listed bodies are not the ordinary first appellate forum under the Act.

questions.subject: Costing
questions.prompt: A firm sells its product for ₹250 per unit. Variable cost is ₹150 per unit and total fixed cost is ₹4,00,000. How many units must it sell to earn a target profit of ₹2,00,000?
questions.explanation: Contribution per unit is ₹250−₹150=₹100. Required units=(₹4,00,000+₹2,00,000)/₹100=6,000, so C is correct.

questions.prompt: A company has current assets of ₹6,00,000 and current liabilities of ₹3,00,000. It pays ₹1,00,000 to trade creditors using cash. What is the new current ratio?

questions.subject: Management
questions.prompt: According to Herzberg's two-factor theory, an organisation substantially improves salary administration, physical working conditions and company policies. Which result is most consistent with the theory?
options: Dissatisfaction may decline, without necessarily increasing positive motivation
Hygiene factors automatically replace all motivators
questions.explanation: Salary, policies and working conditions are hygiene factors in Herzberg's model: improving them can reduce dissatisfaction without necessarily creating positive motivation. Hence B.

questions.prompt: An existing conventional fixed-coupon bond has no change in its promised cash flows or default risk. If the market-required yield increases, its market price will ordinarily:
questions.explanation: For an existing fixed-coupon bond, price and required yield ordinarily move inversely, all else equal. A higher required yield therefore lowers price. Hence B.

questions.prompt: The standard material price is ₹70 per kg, the actual price is ₹65 per kg, and actual quantity purchased and used is 500 kg. What is the material price variance, using the standard cost minus actual cost convention?

questions.subject: Commerce & Accountancy
questions.prompt: A business sells goods for ₹80,000 on credit in the current accounting period. Ignore GST and cost of goods sold. Which is the immediate accounting effect under accrual accounting?

Trade receivables and revenue both increase by ₹80,000

No accounting entry arises until payment is received

questions.subject: Commerce & Accountancy
questions.prompt: A company incurs ₹40,000 of wages relating to work completed in March, but pays the workers in April. Its accounting year ends on 31 March. Under accrual accounting, the March year-end financial statements should ordinarily:
options: Recognise neither an expense nor a liability until April
Recognise a wages expense and corresponding outstanding liability
Recognise an expense only when the bank balance decreases
questions.explanation: Accrual accounting recognises the March wages expense when earned by workers and an outstanding liability until paid. Hence B.

questions.prompt: A company produces 1,000 units and sells 800 units in a period, with no opening inventory. Fixed production overhead is fully absorbed at ₹100 per unit. All other accounting treatments are identical. How does absorption-costing profit compare with marginal-costing profit?

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Assuming effective monetary-policy transmission and other conditions unchanged, a reduction in the policy repo rate by the RBI would generally tend to:
options: Increase borrowing costs and reduce aggregate demand
Reduce borrowing costs and support interest-sensitive spending
Automatically increase every commercial bank's lending rate by the same amount
Have no possible influence on investment or consumption
questions.explanation: With effective transmission, a repo-rate reduction generally lowers borrowing costs and supports interest-sensitive spending; it does not mechanically force every bank rate to move one-for-one. Hence B.
